mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved from -79.6 to -74.4 over the last four weeks, a consistent recovery trend. Persistence of this trend implies continued improvement over the next four weeks as consumers resume pre-lockdown shopping and leisure habits.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -79.6 to -74.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the recovery trend stalled or reversed.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility recovers by more than 4 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, it signals an official easing of workplace restrictions that will also permit more retail and recreation activity within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 4 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -58.0 to -54.1 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses the threshold improvement in two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates restored commuting and work routines; the combined effect of more people traveling and working outside the home compounds to increase incidental retail visits more than either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -74.3 to -66.9 and WORKPLACES from -64.0 to -54.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than what a single-series (TRANSIT or WORKPLACES only) linear model would predict, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The continued rise in PARKS mobility during the warming summer season reflects increased outdoor leisure activity, which in a summer reopening regime spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits (e.g., shopping after park outings), raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -43.7 to -29.6 over four weeks
regime_hint: summer reopening with eased outdoor restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite PARKS continuing to rise, or PARKS and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily improved, reflecting normalization of essential shopping patterns; this week-to-week momentum is a leading indicator that non-essential retail visits (RETAIL_REC) will rise in the immediate next week as overall mobility confidence grows.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -39.1 to -32.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the week immediately following does not increase even though GROCERY_PHARM continued its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 15 points above baseline, it indicates people are spending meaningfully less time at home, a behavioral shift that frees time and willingness for retail and recreation trips, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 23.3 to 19.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks even after RESIDENTIAL crosses below the 15-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in TRANSIT mobility of more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks signals a policy-driven restoration of public transport capacity, which in a phased transport reopening regime directly enables more retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -70.4 to -66.9 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing the specified threshold improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS reflects a broad-based societal reopening where commuting, outdoor activity, and work resumption reinforce one another, producing a compounded and more durable rise in RETAIL_REC than any single series would predict over four weeks, regardless of the specific policy regime in place.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series improved monotonically or near-monotonically over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days matches or falls below what a model using only the strongest single predictor series would forecast, indicating no synergistic interaction.
